title: Step of the call-stopping wrapper
statement: Let $C$ be a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, with designated states $\mathrm{entry}$ and $\mathrm{exit}$. For a Boolean input word $x$, a configuration $c$ of $C$ on $x$, and a flag $b\in\{0,1\}$, suppose that $c$ is live and that $c$ is not in state $\mathrm{exit}$ whenever $b=1$. One step of the wrapper machine, from the configuration formed by adjoining flag $b$ to $c$, yields the configuration formed by adjoining flag $1$ to the result of one step of $C$ from $c$.
hypotheses_covered: $C$ is a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet
Designated entry and exit states of $C$
replaced:
If the embedded configuration is live and not (with the flag raised) at the
designated exit, then one step of the call-stopping wrapper performs the same
physical step as the wrapped machine and raises the release flag.
